methods.label: Express the balance in interest-sized parts
methods.explanation:
Simple interest for two months is \(2/12\) of a year's interest. Let \(P\) be the original principal and \(I\) the credited interest, both in dollars. Then
\[
I=P\cdot\frac{5}{100}\cdot\frac{2}{12}
 =\frac{P}{120}.
\]
Thus the principal is \(120I\). Adding the interest makes the final balance \(121I\), so
\[
121I=255.31,
\qquad
I=\frac{255.31}{121}=2.11.
\]
The credited interest was \(2\) dollars and \(\boxed{11}\) cents, choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
